name: NeoHorse-Jev-4B
description: A 4B structured decision model using prefill-only inference to output probabilities over application-defined Choice, Noul, and Score answers, enabling routing, tool selection, and rating in agent workflows, with local deployment via vLLM, SGLang, or native runtimes.

name: jevons-lfm25-1.2b-systemone
description: A LoRA adapter for LiquidAI's LFM2.5-1.2B-Instruct (8-bit MLX) that biases outputs toward option-key, yes/no, and score-digit tokens so the jevons server can logit-score and assemble System One decisions, with a 72.4% holdout modal accuracy at T=1.

name: CLM-v0.1-8B
description: CLM-v0.1-8B is a contrastive "System One" model that trains small state and action projection heads over a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder to score and rank candidates for agentic decision-making, with separable state/action embeddings enabling caching for up to 13× faster inference.

name: JEV-27B
description: An open dual-mode model serving calibrated typed decisions (yes/no, 2–16-option choice, 0–5 scores) in one forward pass and ordinary Qwen3.8-27B text generation from a single set of weights in one vLLM engine, while reproducing TypeSafe Jev 1.13's output distributions to within ~0.017 KL.

name: gliner2.5-cua-grounder-macos-v1
description: A merged FP32 GLiNER2.5 fine-tune that chooses an action ID, `reobserve`, or `abstain` from a bounded action menu for local macOS CUA automation—without screenshots or tool calls—and is verified on browser DOM and native AppKit fixtures with low-latency MPS inference.

name: openjev
description: openjev fine-tunes Qwen3.5 into a zero-shot NLI cross-encoder (4B text+image v2, plus a 35B-A3B MoE variant) that scores premise–hypothesis pairs as entailment/contradiction/neutral — one primitive for reranking, answer grading, content guarding, and driving real-time game agents like Doom and Minecraft.

name: laya-grounded
description: A fine-tune of the laya typed-decision model that improves grounding on explicitly stated facts, consistency between logical inverses, and probability calibration, at the cost of worse phishing detection and option-name routing stability.

name: rsi-jev-v6.1-vl-27b
description: A 26.66B-parameter typed-decision vision-language model—a weight average of two Qwen3.8-27B fine-tunes—that returns calibrated per-option probabilities for choice/noul/score questions over text and up to four images in one forward pass, early-exiting at layers 48/56/64.

name: safe-laya
description: safe-laya is an Apache-2.0 421M ModernBERT decision model that scores untrusted prompts, retrieved docs, and tool outputs for prompt-injection/jailbreak risk in one ~30ms local pass—a cheap, private injection-guard signal with signed AI-BOM and reproducible training.

name: Open-Jev-9B
description: Open-Jev-9B is a LoRA adapter plus scalar decision head for Qwen3.5-9B that scores caller-supplied candidates and returns typed choice/yes-no/ordinal decisions with calibrated probabilities—without autoregressive generation—via a pinned-revision inference server.

name: basal-1.0-4.5B
description: basal-1.0-4.5B is a 4.5B-parameter Polish/English model that answers typed questions (choice, yes/no, score) about a state by returning calibrated per-option probabilities in one forward pass, enabling fast dynamic classification with confidence-thresholded auto-acceptance.

name: Open-Jev-27B-v1.1
description: A 15.5M-parameter LoRA adapter and scalar decision head for Qwen3.8-27B that scores supplied candidates and returns typed choice, yes/no, and ordinal-score probabilities without autoregressive generation, scoring 85.28% on 231 public JevBench tasks (72.07% Hard).

name: OneJev
description: OneJev is a multimodal System One decision model (0.8B–27B) that reads screenshots, photos, video, or text and returns calibrated probabilities for every option of every question in one shared forward pass, serving TypeSafe's System One API for fast GUI-agent decisions.

name: clef-flash
description: Clef-Flash is a 9B multimodal model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B that maps a state (text, JSON, images, or video) plus a schema of typed questions to per-option probabilities for every question in a single forward pass, with no free-form generation or parsing.

name: laya-GGUF
description: GGML-compiled via ggmlc (not llama.cpp-compatible) F16/Q8_0/Q4_K_M weights of the 421M ModernBERT-based Laya English System-1 decision model, scoring typed choice/score/noul questions in one encoder pass for email routing, injection guards, and agent gating.

name: Sev-4B
description: Sev-4B is a Qwen3.5-4B LoRA adapter with a decision head that scores candidate answers about security logs and recovered programs—including authorization-policy checks grounded in real code—giving analysts calibrated evidence review (84.0% held-out policy accuracy) without generating text.

name: basal-1.0-1.5B
description: basal-1.0-1.5B is a 1.5B-parameter Polish/English decision model distilled from basal-1.0-4.5B that, given a state and a typed question (choice, yes/no, or score) with options defined in plain language, returns calibrated per-option probabilities in a single forward pass — enabling dynamic, retraining-free classification, routing, and triage at ~2× lower latency than its teacher.

name: JEVision
description: JEVision is a Qwen3.5-0.8B-based System One decision stack with text and visual LoRA adapters, pointer heads, and a local runtime that accepts text plus optional images and returns typed Choice, Noul, or Score answers through one API.

name: autojev-27b
description: AutoJev-27B is a 27B-parameter multimodal decision model finetuned from Qwen3.8-27B that returns calibrated probabilities for supplied choices in a single forward pass, exposes a TypeSafe-compatible API and playground, and improves benchmark accuracy/ECE/Brier over its base.

name: jev-control-es
description: A 149M-parameter ModernBERT-base decision model that scores each option at its own dedicated [MASK] token in a single bidirectional pass, returning calibrated softmax probabilities for agent-harness decision sites (injection gates, tool routing, context ranking, sufficiency, escalation) at ~7.7 ms per decision.

name: Julia-1
description: Julia-1 is a 144.3M-parameter multilingual decision model built on mmBERT-small that maps a state, a typed question, and 2–20 supplied options to a scored choice, rubric score, or Boolean probability for routing and typed-decision workloads.

name: ModernJEV-Decide-Preview
description: A 149.6M-parameter ModernBERT cross-encoder fine-tuned on 60,000 agent decisions that scores and ranks user-supplied candidate labels, given a conversation, policy, and tool descriptions, for next-action routing and tool selection within 4,096-token inputs.

name: lev
description: lev is a LoRA adapter on Qwen3.5-4B that answers typed yes/no, choice, and score questions about a state in one batched forward pass, returning calibrated probabilities over your options with zero output tokens for routing, moderation, triage, and gating decisions.

name: vera-deberta-v3-large
description: VERA is a fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large model that scores and ranks candidate headline or short-copy variants by predicted click rate in a single forward pass, trained on 62,695 arms from 32,487 real A/B tests to pick higher-performing variants without generation or prompting.

name: rlcd-modernbert-151m
description: A 151M-parameter ModernBERT-based decision engine delivering calibrated choices, scores, and probabilities—plus an explicit abstention slot—in a single ~35ms non-autoregressive forward pass, deployable in-browser via WebGPU/WASM or via ONNX for edge inference.

name: Jeff-1
description: Jeff-1 is an Apache-2.0 LoRA adapter for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 that scores caller-supplied labels to return typed decisions—choice, yes/no, and ordinal scores with probabilities and confidence—for local inference tasks like fact-checking without parsing generated text.

name: ArseneLupin-mini-v1.0
description: ArseneLupin-mini-v1.0 is a 0.87B-parameter decision model (Qwen3.5-0.8B + merged LoRA and a trained read-out head) that returns calibrated probability distributions for yes/no, choice, and score questions over any input state in one forward pass per option, with no text generation, served via a System One-compatible API in bf16 or GGUF Q8_0.

name: kev-4b
description: Kev-4B is a LoRA adapter plus pointer head on Qwen3.5-4B-Base that maps a document and typed questions to calibrated per-question probability distributions in one forward pass—no generation—serving TypeSafe's /v1/systemone decision contract at 0.837 out-of-domain locked-test accuracy.

name: spark-s1-1.7b-v3
description: spark-s1-1.7b-v3 is a LoRA-tuned Qwen3-1.7B decision model that answers typed questions (choice, boolean, score) over request-time options by softmaxing first-token logits into a probability distribution and confidence in one ~30 ms forward pass, with no text generation.

name: Intern-Decision-4B
description: Intern-Decision-4B is a multimodal Qwen3.5-4B fine-tune that scores every field of a typed decision schema (choice, score, or binary, with up to 8 images) in a single calibrated forward pass—returning per-option probability distributions without generation—achieving a 90.02 benchmark average at ~44 ms per query on an RTX 4090.

name: Winnow-E4B
description: Winnow-E4B is a compact merged-GGUF Gemma 4 E4B fine-tune that scores supplied answer options for yes/no, choice, and score questions over a shared state—returning probabilities without generating text—while keeping chat and image support for fast local decisions.

name: laya
description: Laya is an Apache-2.0 multilingual non-autoregressive decision model that answers typed questions (choices, scores, booleans) over text or JSON states with calibrated probabilities in a single ~33 ms forward pass, auto-routing across three checkpoints covering 100+ languages.

name: jev-berta-base-zeroshot-classifier
description: DeBERTa-v3-base model that scores variable-length candidate choices against a context and query, using candidate-set self-attention so each option is judged conditioned on all alternatives, and a JEV adapter mapping state, instructions, and criteria to predictions per question.

name: openjevx
description: OpenJevX is a small CPU-first ONNX decision model (8-bit, 598 MB) that answers yes/no, pick-one, and 0–N rating questions about a JSON or text state with per-answer probabilities and confidence, running fully locally via Docker or Python at ~22–540 ms CPU latency.

name: zeiger-0.6b
description: Zeiger-0.6B is a 614M-parameter encoder-decision model (Qwen3-0.6B backbone plus 18M scoring head) that, given a web page's element descriptions and an instruction, picks the target element—or answers "none"—in one calibrated 32k-context forward pass at up to 1,501 candidates, enabling fast, reliable browser-agent element grounding without generation or chunked tournaments.

name: rsi-jev-v2.0-qwen3.5-2b
description: rsi-jev-v2.0-qwen3.5-2b is a Qwen3.5-2B typed-decision model that answers yes/no, pick-one, and rubric-score questions about documents in one forward pass, returning calibrated per-option probabilities for trustworthy automated decisions and escalation routing.

name: agent-jev
description: AgentJev-0.6B turns a 2,048-token state and typed boolean, choice, or score questions into full probability distributions in one forward pass, giving agent loops fast, thresholdable gates, routes, and rubric scores without decoded text, JSON repair, or a larger writer model.

name: spark-s1-4b-v3
description: spark-s1-4b-v3 is a Qwen3-4B LoRA fine-tune that answers typed questions (choice, boolean, ordered score) about a rendered state by softmaxing first-token logits over option letters—returning a calibrated per-option probability distribution plus confidence in one forward pass with no text generation—for fast local agent decisions.

name: decider-2b
description: decider-2b is a 1.9B-parameter model that returns calibrated probability distributions over explicit option lists for multiple typed questions in one forward pass—no text generation—for fast routing, classification, judgments, and agent decisions.

name: JEV-27B-VL
description: JEV-27B-VL adds vision to JEV-27B as an adapter on Qwen3.8-27B, outputting calibrated probabilities for typed decisions (yes/no, 2–16 options, 0–5 ratings) over images and text in one forward pass — enabling zero-shot cold-start video recommendation and benchmark-topping agent/multimodal judging.

name: Jeff-Qwen3.5-0.8B
description: Jeff-Qwen3.5-0.8B is an Apache-2.0 fine-tune of Qwen3.5-0.8B that turns arbitrary states and plain-language options into calibrated per-option probabilities in a single ~22 ms forward pass, enabling fast local zero-shot classification, routing, and game-playing decisions.

name: cua-s1-forms
description: cua-s1-forms is a 706K-parameter single-pass option scorer that maps a GUI form element plus typed candidates (fill each extracted entity, check, click, skip) to per-option probabilities, letting cua-driver fill and submit forms without an autoregressive LLM.

name: matilda-jev-v1
description: A 26.1B-parameter decision model that returns temperature-calibrated probabilities over the options of choice, yes/no, and scored-rubric questions in a single deterministic forward pass—no sampling or answer parsing—scoring 59.26 on the Jev Decision Index.

name: Winnow-12B
description: Winnow-12B is a GGUF-packaged LoRA fine-tune of Gemma 4 12B IT for local inference, providing typed decisions (noul, choice, score) via shared-state logit reads without generating answer text, plus ordinary chat and vision, in BF16 and Q8_0 variants tested at 64K context on a 16 GB GPU.

name: verdict
description: Verdict is a small trained head over frozen SigLIP 2 that answers typed image questions—multiple-choice with an "other" abstention and true/false statements—in a single forward pass, returning calibrated per-option probabilities with no text generation.

name: tasksource-jev-nano-v0
description: Tasksource-JEV-Nano-v0 is a 149M-parameter ColBERT-style late-interaction model (fine-tuned from LateOn on 512k typed decisions) that picks the best option from a list—choice, yes/no, or graded scoring—with a cacheable situation encoding and permutation-equivariant option scoring instead of a classifier head.

name: gev-e2b
description: Gev-e2b pairs a LoRA adapter and pointer head on Gemma 4 E2B to score options for choice, yes/no, and ordinal questions, outputting one answer with a calibrated probability distribution (82.9% trained-source, 62.5% new-source accuracy).

name: ArseneLupinstral-v1.0
description: ArseneLupinstral-v1.0 is an Apache-2.0, 8.92B-parameter Mistral Ministral-3-8B decision model whose merged LoRA and trained readout head turn a supplied state and yes/no, choice, or score questions into calibrated probability distributions—one forward pass per option, no generated text—via a System One-style API.

name: jev-control-core
description: jev-control-core is a fully fine-tuned 0.8B decoder that answers typed choice/score questions at embedded agent-harness decision sites (tool routing, injection gates, triage, escalation) in one restricted-option forward pass, yielding calibrated confidence at ~18.5ms per decision.

name: vjev-vision
description: vjev-vision is a Qwen3.5-4B-based listwise decision model that, given text and image states plus typed questions (noul, choice, score), returns calibrated probabilities for every option in a single forward pass without text generation.

name: pplx-decider-v1.1-27b
description: Apache-2.0 Qwen3.8-27B finetune for scored candidate decisions, shipping a Qwen3_5Model backbone with a separate BF16 [255,5120] readout, noncausal full-attention behavior, and calibrated predict code that raises Decision Index to 61.56 (v1: 56.4, Jev: 57.9).

name: rsi-jev-v6.0-vl-4b
description: rsi-jev-v6.0-vl-4b is a 4.69B-parameter vision-language decision model fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-4B-Base that answers typed questions (yes/no, multiple-choice, rubric scores) about text plus up to four images in a single reasoning-free forward pass, returning calibrated per-option probabilities via early-exit heads at layers 16, 20, and 32 for adaptive compute.

name: GEV-26B-Decide
description: A LoRA adapter on Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (≈4B active parameters) that returns calibrated probabilities for typed decisions—yes/no, 2–256 options, 0–5 ratings—over text and images in one ~45 ms pass, optionally escalating uncertain cases to System 2 reasoning for higher accuracy.

name: rsi-jev-v4.0-vl-qwen3.5-2b
description: A 2B typed-decision model built on Qwen3.5-2B-Base with a trained option-scoring head that returns calibrated per-option probabilities for yes/no, pick-one-of-k, and rubric-score questions about a document plus up to four images in a single forward pass, generating no text.

name: ArseneLupin-v1.1
description: ArseneLupin-v1.1 is an Apache-2.0 decision model fine-tuned (merged LoRA) from Qwen3.5-4B that returns calibrated probability distributions for typed yes/no, choice, and scored questions over a given state in a single forward pass per option, served via a System One-style API in full bfloat16 (transformers) or 8-bit GGUF (llama.cpp) form.

name: Rook-V1
description: Rook-V1 is an uncalibrated self-hosted research decision model for bounded choices, routing, and candidate scoring, providing a LoRA adapter, decision head, tokenizer, configs, reload code, integrity manifest, and evaluation artifacts for reconstruction on the pinned Lux 9B.

name: jeeves
description: Jeeves-9B is a fused Qwen3.5-9B decision model that writes a reasoning chain for each yes/no, multiple-choice, or rating question about a given state and returns calibrated per-option probabilities, bundled with a pointer head, fitted temperature, and two diffusion drafters for faster serving.

name: K2-Type-0.9B
description: K2-Type-0.9B is a 0.9B non-generative decision model that scores every option of typed yes/no, multiple-choice, and ordinal questions against one shared text/JSON state with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass (JevBench public 176/231, ~27 ms median).

name: jebadiah-9b-v0
description: Jebadiah-9B-v0 is an Apache-2.0 LoRA adapter on Qwen3.5-9B-Base that answers typed decision questions (choice, yes/no "noul", rubric score) by emitting a calibrated probability distribution over option-label tokens instead of generating text, trained on 11,072 public questions and served via AINode's /v1/decide and /v1/systemone routes.

name: chessjev-minilm-v1
description: A chess option scorer that finetunes MiniLM-L6 with an attention head to emit logits for all legal moves from a FEN context in one forward pass, distilled from Stockfish 19 (0.445 teacher agreement, 0.667 on tactics) for fast move ranking rather than verified playing strength.

name: THX-01
description: THX-01 is a 322M-parameter non-autoregressive multilingual decision model that answers typed natural-language questions—choices, yes/no, ordinal scores, numbers, verbatim excerpts, and citations—about a given document or state in a single ~10 ms pass, returning calibrated probabilities trained via RL on strictly proper scoring rules.

name: Open-Jev-2B
description: A LoRA adapter and scalar decision head for Qwen3.5-2B that directly scores caller-supplied candidates and returns calibrated typed decisions—choice probabilities, yes/no probability, or ordinal expected values—without autoregressive generation, achieving 94.71% test and 86.02% OOD hard accuracy.

name: drex-dlm
description: Drex DLM is an 8B diffusion-language decision model that answers typed questions—named choices, yes/no, and ordinal scales—about a supplied context in a single forward pass plus pointer head, returning option probabilities for agentic routing and decision tasks.

name: JEV
description: An open-weights 9B decision model (Qwen3.5-9B backbone with a LoRA-tuned 24-slot linear head) distilled from TypeSafe Jev 1.13 that returns calibrated probability distributions for yes/no, 2–16-option choice, and 0–5 score questions in a single forward pass.

name: spark-s1-4b-v6
description: spark-s1-4b-v6 is a LoRA-merged Qwen3.5-4B System-1 decision model that, given a state and a typed question, returns calibrated probabilities over lettered options in one forward pass — useful for fast local agent guardrails such as allow/ask/deny tool-call decisions.

name: hotdog-27B
description: hotdog-27B is a rank-16 LoRA adapter on Qwen3.8-27B that answers yes/no questions about text with a probability and binary decision read directly from logits, achieving 98.28% independent-test accuracy and strong calibration without generating reasoning.

name: On-Fly-Jev
description: On-Fly-Jev is a 96M-parameter PyTorch typed-decision model built on a spiking neural network trunk of 100 real Drosophila MaleCNS connectome neurons, returning calibrated probabilities for choice/score/noul questions in a single forward pass at ~137 decisions per second (7.3 ms p50) with best-in-group 0.045 ECE.

name: jev-schema-scorer-deberta-v3-large
description: A fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large encoder with a scalar head that scores (state, question + candidate) pairs, decoding grouped logits via softmax into choice, boolean (noul), and ordinal score answers—reading criteria and option ids at inference time so one checkpoint handles new label sets without retraining.

name: NanoJev
description: NanoJev is a 0.6B Qwen3-based decision model whose shared backbone and attention Choice head score each state/question-encoded candidate set and return action distributions via softmax—without output-token decoding—for Maze, Snake, ViZDoom Basic, and Predict Position through a structured interface.

name: pplx-decider-v1-27b
description: pplx-decider-v1-27b is an Apache-2.0 PyTorch decision model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B that predicts labeled choices or yes/no answers with calibrated probabilities, supports image inputs, and reaches 85.71% overall accuracy across 11 benchmarks.

name: laya-typed-decisions
description: A 421M-parameter non-autoregressive ModernBERT-large model, RLCD-fine-tuned to emit calibrated probability distributions over typed primitives (choice, score, noul) for four workflows—agent observability, customer service, invoicing, security incidents—at 0.766 accuracy.

name: Tev1-4B-experimental
description: Tev1-4B-experimental is an experimental supervised fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B that answers structured decision tasks, returning exactly one option letter given a state, question, and 2–24 labeled choices via a standard next-token head under deterministic decoding.

name: noma
description: An open decision model on a truncated Qwen3.5-4B backbone that returns calibrated per-option probabilities plus abstain and uncertainty for typed questions in ~16 ms, enabling fast routing, triage, scoring, and agent-step verification without text generation.

name: Jev-Omni
description: Jev-Omni is an Apache-2.0 multimodal decision classifier built on Gemma 4 12B IT that returns calibrated per-option probabilities for text, image, audio, and video questions, scoring 63.10% on MMAU and 53.10% on MVBench with millisecond-scale inference.

name: clef-flash-4bit
description: clef-flash-4bit is a 4-bit MLX quantization of Cloudflare's 9B clef-flash for Apple Silicon whose bundled clef_mlx.py loader (CLI or local SystemOne server) maps a text/JSON/image/video state plus a schema of typed questions to option probabilities in a single forward pass.

name: Blink-v0.3-26B-A4B-NVFP4
description: Blink-v0.3-26B-A4B-NVFP4 is a Gemma-4-based MoE decision model (4B active params, NVFP4, 32k context) that returns calibrated per-option probabilities in a single forward pass, replacing "ask an LLM and parse prose" calls for routing, moderation, tagging, gating, dedup, and yes/no checks.

name: JEV-9B
description: JEV-9B is an open dual-mode model that adds a 40.2M-parameter decision adapter to a frozen Qwen3.5-9B backbone, returning calibrated probability distributions for typed decisions (yes/no, 2–16 choices, 0–5 scores) in ~90 ms while leaving base generation byte-identical.

name: MedJev-Qwen3.5-0.8B
description: MedJev-Qwen3.5-0.8B is a LoRA adapter plus pointer head on Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base that extracts 11 predefined clinical variables from free-text clinical notes in a single forward pass (~62 ms per note), returning calibrated probability distributions over allowed answers without text generation, achieving 0.878 micro accuracy against silver GPT-4-derived labels.

name: ballot
description: ballot-E-v0 is a ~149M-parameter ModernBERT fine-tune that returns per-option probabilities for multiple-choice, yes/no, or rating questions in one non-generative forward pass, structurally guaranteeing order-invariant answers (0.0% flip rate) at 68% held-out accuracy.

name: open-jev-deberta-v3-large
description: A DeBERTa-v3-large encoder that maps one input state plus any number of typed questions (choice, ordered score, or yes/no) to calibrated per-question probability distributions in a single forward pass, reaching 0.854 in-domain accuracy at 0.022 ECE with zero structured-output errors.

name: APUS-OpenJev-v1
description: APUS-OpenJev-v1 is a family of Qwen3.5-based decision models (4B, 9B, 35B-A3B) that score candidate actions for browser agents and business workflows, offering selectable low/high compute depth, candidate-aware output projection, and English-Chinese support.

name: clef
description: Clef is a 27B multimodal model post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B that maps a state (text, JSON, images, or video) plus a schema of typed questions (true/false, choice, or score) to per-option probabilities for every question in a single forward pass—no free-form generation or output parsing—via a joint schema head and a Jev/SystemOne-compatible API.

name: h2o-lightning-4b
description: H2O-Lightning-4B is a 4B-parameter multimodal decision model (built on Qwen3.5-4B) that answers choice, yes/no, and ordinal-score questions about text records and attached images in one forward pass returning calibrated per-option probabilities, ranking #1 on JevBench's open-weight composite while running on stock vLLM via a lightweight shim at ~$0.021 per 1,000 decisions.

name: Tev1-0.8B-experimental
description: Tev1-0.8B-experimental is a 0.8B-parameter supervised fine-tune of Qwen3.5-0.8B that, given a structured prompt containing a state, question, and 2–24 labeled options, deterministically returns a single option letter—making it useful as a lightweight decision/classification layer where application code maps letters back to semantic keys.

name: Jev-Omni-Q4_K_M-GGUF
description: A Q4_K_M GGUF quantization of the Jev-Omni 12B multimodal decision classifier that, together with its original-precision projector and FP32 decision head, lets llama.cpp return option probabilities over text, image, audio, and video inputs on CPU or GPU.

name: JEV-CPU
description: JEV-CPU is a CPU-only port of the SemIf semantic-if engine that loads Qwen3-0.6B in float32 and returns typed option probabilities read directly from option-letter logits in a single forward pass—no GPU or text generation—exposed via CLI and a dependency-free web UI.

name: jebadiah-9b-v2
description: Jebadiah-9b-v2 is a merged bf16 LoRA finetune of Qwen3.5-9B that answers typed choice, yes/no, and rubric-score questions by returning calibrated probability distributions over option labels instead of generating text, served via AINode's /v1/decide and /v1/systemone routes.

name: ballot-jev-0.5b
description: ballot-jev-0.5b is a 506M-parameter CPU-first typed-decision model that returns calibrated full probability distributions for choice, true/false, and ordinal questions, and is structurally permutation-invariant—reordering options provably cannot change its answer.
